{{Short description|Mathematical symbol to denote a function}}
{{For|the butterfly called a maplet|Chersonesia{{!}}''Chersonesia''}}
{{Infobox punctuation mark|mark=↦}}

The '''maps to''' symbol, ↦, is a rightward arrow protruding from a vertical bar.  It is used in [[mathematics]] and in [[computer science]]<ref>Specifically [[Functional Programming]]</ref> to denote [[Function (mathematics)|function]]s.
* In [[Z notation]], a [[specification language]] used in software development,<ref>
{{cite book
|last=Mikušiak |first=Luboš
|author2=Miroslav Adámy
|author3=Thomas Seidmann
|title=TAPSOFT '97: Theory and Practice of Software Development
|chapter=Publishing formal specifications in Z notation on world wide web
|series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science
|year=1997|volume=1214 |pages=871–874
|doi=10.1007/BFb0030650 |isbn=978-3-540-62781-4 |doi-access=free
}}</ref> this symbol is called the '''maplet arrow''' and the expression x ↦ y is called a '''maplet'''.
* In [[separation logic]] it denotes the contents of a specific cell of memory.


In the [[Unicode]] character set, the symbol is code point U+21A6.<ref>[https://www.fileformat.info/info/unicode/char/21a6/index.htm Unicode Character 'RIGHTWARDS ARROW FROM BAR' (U+21A6)<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>
<br>


== Other uses ==
The "Maps to" operator is useful when it is desirable to avoid assigning names to functions.  

This can avoid possible misinterpretations due to poor naming conventions,<ref>
See [[Anonymous_function| Lambda Functions]] in [[Python (programming language)]]
</ref> such as avoiding the following name conflict from these two functions existing in the same file or in the same mathematical proof:
* <code>func sqr: </code><math> x \mapsto x*x </math>
** Squares the input value
* <code>func sqr: </code><math> x \mapsto (2*x)+(2*x) </math>.
** Calculates the perimeter of a square when given an input side length.
